tools.name: deployments_list
tools.description: List every deployment you can access (owned + shared). The `owned` flag tells them apart. Pass name to find one by name, and brief: true when you only need to pick one: it returns id, name, state, url, runtime and entry file instead of the full record.

tools.name: deployments_get
tools.description: Fetch a single deployment.

tools.name: deployments_update
tools.description: Rename a deployment.

tools.name: deployments_move
tools.description: Move a deployment to another of your projects.

tools.name: deployments_delete
tools.description: Delete a deployment (instant; teardown runs in the background).

tools.name: deployments_create
tools.description: Create a deployment (blank, from a public GitHub repo, or a template), or a database by passing its engine as `runtime`. Sized by default to an equal share of the free pool; the result tells you the RAM/CPU it got. A modern web stack needs 512+ MB to npm install (exit 137 = OOM): deployments.resize

tools.name: deployments_getStartup
tools.description: Get the startup config: runtime, version, entry file, start command.

tools.name: deployments_updateStartup
tools.description: Change runtime / version / entry file / start command (queues a rebuild). The start command is a FULL SHELL LINE run at every boot: it can install and build before starting - e.g. 'npm install && npm run build && exec node build/index.js'. There is no other way to run build steps, and there does not

tools.name: runtimes_list
tools.description: List available runtimes, services and database engines with their versions.

tools.name: deployments_getGit
tools.description: Get the linked GitHub source: repo, branch, auto-pull.

tools.name: deployments_setAutoPull
tools.description: Toggle auto-pull: re-pull the linked repo on every restart.

tools.name: deployments_power
tools.description: Send a power signal (start / stop / restart / kill). A start or a restart WAITS for the process to settle and hands back the state it reached, the console output it produced and what to do about it: ok:true only means the signal was accepted, the logs say whether the app actually came up. Never anno

tools.name: deployments_logs
tools.description: Read the last N lines of the console log, cleaned of colour codes and progress spam. A build or install takes MINUTES: pass waitSeconds (e.g. 25) to wait server-side before reading, instead of calling this again and again - polling in a loop is how a whole conversation gets eaten by npm output. tools.name: deployments_searchLogs
tools.description: Find lines in the console log that deployments.logs does not show: it searches the last 2000 lines (up to 5000) for a word or a regular expression, case-insensitive, and returns each hit with a few lines around it. Use it when the tail looks fine but something went wrong earlier, or to find the firs

tools.name: deployments_resources
tools.description: Live resource usage: CPU, memory, disk, network and uptime.

tools.name: deployments_command
tools.description: Write a line to the running process's stdin (a game server console, a REPL). NOT a shell: a web server ignores stdin, so curl / node / npm typed here do nothing, and no output is returned. To run a command (curl, node, npm, grep) use deployments.shell; to request a public URL, deployments.check.

tools.name: deployments_resize
tools.description: Change RAM / CPU / storage allocation (drawn from your plan pool). The deployment restarts to apply it.

tools.name: deployments_sync
tools.description: Pull the latest code from the linked GitHub repo (restarts it if it was running). Pass branch, and repo if it changed, to FIX a wrong branch after a failed clone: that repoints the deployment and pulls, and is the way to recover, never deleting and recreating.

tools.name: deployments_diagnose
tools.description: Everything needed to answer "what is wrong with this deployment", in ONE call: live state, RAM and CPU, the cleaned log tail, the startup config, and what the public URL returns. Use this INSTEAD of the deployments.get + deployments.logs + deployments.check + deployments.getStartup sequence - it rep

tools.name: deployments_apply
tools.description: Make edited files live and confirm they work, in ONE call. Use this after writing files instead of deployments.power + deployments.logs + deployments.check. It restarts only when the runtime needs it (a static or PHP site serves straight off the volume, so the restart is skipped and `skippedRestart`

tools.name: files_list
tools.description: List a directory inside the deployment volume.

tools.name: files_tree
tools.description: See the whole project layout in ONE call: every file and folder under a path, indented, with sizes. Use this FIRST when exploring, instead of walking directories with files.list. It returns structure only - read the files you want with files.readMany. Dependency folders (node_modules, vendor, .git,

tools.name: files_readMany
tools.description: Read SEVERAL files in one call. Pair it with files.tree: look at the layout, then pull the handful of files you actually need in a single round instead of one call each. Binary files are reported, never returned as text.

tools.name: files_search
tools.description: Search the text of the project for a string or regex, like grep. Returns matching lines with their file and line number. Use it to find where something is defined or used instead of reading files one by one.

tools.name: files_edit
tools.description: Change PART of a file by replacing an exact snippet, leaving the rest untouched. Prefer this over files.write for any edit to an existing file: rewriting a whole file to change a few lines is slow, expensive and loses anything you did not repeat. The snippet must appear EXACTLY once unless you pass

tools.name: files_editMany
tools.description: Change SEVERAL places in ONE file in a single call. Use this instead of calling files.edit again and again on the same file: each files.edit is another round trip that re-sends the whole conversation. The edits apply in order, all of them or none: if one snippet is missing or ambiguous the file is l

tools.name: files_read
tools.description: Read a file, or a slice of it. Use offset/limit to page through a long file.

tools.name: files_write
tools.description: Create or overwrite a text file. A large file does NOT have to fit in one call: send the first part with mode 'overwrite', then the rest with mode 'append'.

tools.name: files_writeMany
tools.description: Create or overwrite SEVERAL files in ONE call. Use this when creating a project: index.html, style.css and package.json go in a single call instead of one files.write each, which costs a round trip per file. Files are written in the order given; if one fails the call stops and the reply says exactly

tools.name: files_rename
tools.description: Rename or MOVE a file or directory: from and to are paths relative to root, and may point into different directories. To move several items into a folder in one call, use files.move.

tools.name: files_move
tools.description: Move files or folders into a directory of the SAME deployment; the directory is created if missing. Never overwrites: a name already taken there is reported, not replaced. There is no move between two deployments: copying a file across leaves the original, so that is a copy, not a move.

tools.name: files_delete
tools.description: Delete one or more files or folders. A copy of each deleted FILE is kept, so files.history / files.restore can bring it back; a deleted folder is gone for good.

tools.name: files_mkdir
tools.description: Create an EMPTY folder. Not needed before files.move, files.write or files.writeMany: they create the folders they need.

tools.name: files_decompress
tools.description: Decompress an archive in place. With removeArchive the archive is deleted right after, in the same call, so an upload-and-unpack never leaves the archive behind.

tools.name: files_compress
tools.description: Compress files into a new archive.

tools.name: files_copy
tools.description: Duplicate a file in place (the node appends a " copy" suffix). NOT a move: to move or rename, use files.rename.

tools.name: files_chmod
tools.description: Change a file mode (e.g. "0755").

tools.name: files_downloadUrl
tools.description: Get a one-time signed URL to download a file.

tools.name: files_index
tools.description: Flat index of every file under a path with size, mtime and an XXH64 content hash, in ONE call, for sync tools. Honours gitignore patterns. Send the `digest` of a listing you already hold: an unchanged tree answers `unchanged: true` with no entries.

tools.name: files_uploadUrl
tools.description: Get a one-time signed URL to upload files straight to the node, with no size cap from the panel. POST a multipart form with one or more `files` parts to it: each lands in `path` under its own file name. Valid 15 minutes, single use. Pair with files.decompress to unpack an archive.

tools.name: files_history
tools.description: List the saved previous versions of ONE file, newest first. Use it when a change broke something, when the user asks to undo or go back, or before overwriting a file you did not write yourself - then pass a versionId to files.restore. It only covers changes made through this API (write, edit, editMa

tools.name: files_restore
tools.description: Put a file back to one of its saved versions: this is the undo. Use it when an edit broke the app or the user asks to revert, and to bring back a file that was deleted. Call files.history first for the versionId. What it replaces is itself saved, so a restore can be undone in turn.

tools.name: env_list
tools.description: List environment variables. Secret values are masked.

tools.name: env_set
tools.description: Create or update a user environment variable (applies on next restart).

tools.name: env_update
tools.description: Update an existing environment variable: rename it (newKey), change its value, or flip its secret flag. Applies on next restart.

tools.name: env_delete
tools.description: Delete a user environment variable (applies on next restart).

tools.name: env_audit
tools.description: Compare the environment variables SET on the deployment with the ones the code actually reads. Use it right after writing code that needs configuration, and whenever an app crashes on boot for no visible reason: it names the variables the code reads but nothing sets (missing), the ones set but never

tools.name: databases_rotatePassword
tools.description: Generate a new password for a database deployment and restart it to apply it. The old password stops working at once: every app connecting with it loses access until it is updated, so confirm with the user first. Returns the new password in full. tools.name: backups_list
tools.description: List the restore points of a deployment, newest first, and the backup operation in progress.

tools.name: backups_get
tools.description: Fetch one restore point of a deployment.

tools.name: backups_restore
tools.description: Restore a restore point. replace: stops the deployment, puts every file back, starts it again if it was running. subfolder: copies the files into /restored-<date>/ without stopping anything. Runs in the background: poll backups.list.

tools.name: packages_list
tools.description: List packages in the manifest (npm or pip).

tools.name: packages_add
tools.description: Add or update a package in the manifest.

tools.name: packages_remove
tools.description: Remove a package from the manifest.

tools.name: account_get
tools.description: Your profile, credit balance, plan and quota (pool vs used).

tools.name: templates_list
tools.description: Browse the public template catalogue (any author).

tools.name: templates_get
tools.description: Full details + public stats of a single template by slug.

tools.name: projects_list
tools.description: List the projects you own or collaborate on.

tools.name: projects_create
tools.description: Create a project.

tools.name: projects_delete
tools.description: Delete a project and all its deployments (owner only).

tools.name: deployments_enableDomains
tools.description: Assign a subdomain (activate domains). Idempotent.

tools.name: deployments_setSlug
tools.description: Set the subdomain alias (slug).

tools.name: deployments_removeSlug
tools.description: Remove the subdomain alias.

tools.name: deployments_setCustomDomain
tools.description: Attach a custom domain. Returns the DNS verification token.

tools.name: deployments_verifyCustomDomain
tools.description: Check the DNS for the attached custom domain.

tools.name: deployments_removeCustomDomain
tools.description: Detach the custom domain.

tools.name: deployments_check
tools.description: Request this deployment over its public URL and report what came back. tools.name: docs_search
tools.description: Search the Bot-Hosting documentation. Use this before answering any "how do I" question.

tools.name: docs_get
tools.description: Read one documentation page in full, by the slug returned from docs.search.

tools.name: files_outline
tools.description: Map the code WITHOUT reading it: every function, class, export and route with its line number, for one file or a whole folder.
